package.author: Moaid Hathot
package.description: A tiling window manager for Windows, with an animation engine, a status bar, a command palette and a configuration language that tells you when you have made a mistake.
package.installationNotes:
Nothing is running yet. In a new terminal (this one has the PATH it started with):

    shubbak setup

That writes a starter config, registers the window manager to start at logon, and
starts it. Then alt+shift+space opens the palette, and ? inside it lists every key.
`shubbak doctor` checks the install if anything seems off.

Installed the default way, Shubbak lives in Program Files and can tile windows that
belong to elevated programs. Installed with --scope user it is a portable copy under
your profile and cannot; run shubbak-wm elevated if you need those tiled.

Getting started: https://github.com/MoaidHathot/Shubbak/blob/v0.11.0/docs/getting-started.md

en-US.longDescription:
Shubbak tiles windows on Windows. It is named for شبّاك, "window"; the status bar is
Taj (تاج, crown), the command palette is Dalil (دليل, guide) and the watcher that
tells the window manager about the rest of the machine - the camera and the
microphone, so far - is Ayn (عين, eye). Five small executables, compiled ahead of
time, with no runtime to install first.

Layouts are a property of a container rather than of a workspace, so a fibonacci
region can sit inside a columns region with no special case. Available layouts are
splith, splitv, fibonacci, fibonacci-v, fibonacci-mirrored, master-left,
master-right, master-top, master-bottom, grid and monocle.

Configuration is one KDL file, shared by the window manager, the bar, the palette
and the watcher, with diagnostics that point at the problem with a caret rather than
a line number. Mistakes that other window managers accept silently - a regex wrapped
in slashes that therefore never matched, a duplicate binding, a rule that would match
every window - are reported rather than ignored. Contexts layer overrides on the
config while a condition on the desktop holds: a presentation, a docked monitor, a
call with the microphone open.

Windows on inactive workspaces are cloaked rather than hidden, so they still report
as visible to Win32. If Shubbak exits, crashes or is killed, the next run adopts
them and brings them back.

`shubbak inspect` prints every matchable attribute of a window, whether Shubbak
will tile it and why not if it will not, and which rules matched.
en-US.name: Shubbak
